<c>I</c>n illo témpore: Accessérunt ad Jesum Pharisæi tentántes eum, et dicéntes: Si licet hómini dimíttere uxórem suam, quacúmque ex causa? Et réliqua.
<r>Homilía sancti Joánnis Chrysóstomi.</r>
<c>V</c>ide Magístri sapiéntiam: qui, cum interrogátus esset, Si licéret hómini dimíttere uxórem; ne conturbaréntur, ántequam senténtiam proférret, confirmatiónem a Scriptúra pósuit, osténdens Patris sui id esse mandátum: et quod ea, quæ ab ipso sunt dicta de non repudiánda uxóre, non modo non repúgnant, verum étiam valde cum Móyse convéniunt. Considerándum autem est, quod non solum ab opifício, verum étiam ab ipso præcépto senténtiam corróborat. Non enim dixit, Quia virum et mulíerem unam solúmmodo fecit; verum étiam, Quia jussit ut unus uni conjungátur: nam si voluísset álteram étiam condúci uxórem, uni viro creáto multas formásset mulíeres: nunc vero et creatiónis, et sanctiónis modo, unam uni perpétuo conjúngi, et nunquam rescíndi oportére perdócuit.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℣.</r> Immaculátus Dóminus immaculátam sibi fámulam, in hoc fragilitátis córpore pósitam, misericórditer consecrávit. De cujus passióne.

<c>P</c>osse autem nos perpétuam serváre continéntiam osténdit, dicens: Sunt eunúchi, qui se ipsos castravérunt propter regnum cælórum. His ómnibus occúlte ad optándam eligendámque virginitátem indúcit: possíbile namque id esse homínibus, hoc fere modo confírmat: Cógita tecum, si aut a natúra eunúchus esses, aut injúria hóminum sic efféctus, quid fáceres, cum et hujúsmodi voluptáte caréres, et nullam caréndo mercédem consequeréris? Grátias ígitur Deo agas, quia magna præmia, rutilantésque corónas habébis, si ita vives, quemádmodum sine áliquo illi præmio; immo vero multo facílius, tútius, atque jucúndius, tum quia spe retributiónis corroboráris, tum quia consciéntia virtútis gaudes, et ad hæc, non ita ingéntibus cupiditátis flúctibus jactáris.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.

<r>Benedictio.</r> Ad societátem cívium supernórum perdúcat nos Rex Angelórum.

<c>C</c>um ergo de his eunúchis díxerit, qui nisi étiam ipsi mente se contíneant, frustra et incássum tales sunt, ac de his, qui ut cælos nanciscántur, se cóntinent, subjúnxit rursus dicens: Qui potest cápere, cápiat. Ita magis ánimat atque incéndit, vel quia magnitúdinem virtútis osténdit, vel quia inæstimábili misericórdia sua nóluit rem in necessitátem legis conclúdere. Et ad hæc, possíbile id esse monstrat, ut eligéndi cupíditas créscere possit. Sed si electiónis opus est id, ínquies, quómodo incípiens statim dixit, Non omnes cápiunt, sed quibus datum est? Ut singuláre id esse certámen perdíscas, non ut sorte datam necessitátem suspicéris.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.

Cum ergo de his eunúchis díxerit, qui nisi étiam ipsi mente se contíneant, frustra et incássum tales sunt, ac de his, qui ut cælos nanciscántur, se cóntinent, subjúnxit rursus dicens: Qui potest cápere, cápiat. Ita magis ánimat atque incéndit, vel quia magnitúdinem virtútis osténdit, vel quia inæstimábili misericórdia sua nóluit rem in necessitátem legis conclúdere. Et ad hæc, possíbile id esse monstrat, ut eligéndi cupíditas créscere possit. Sed si electiónis opus est id, ínquies, quómodo incípiens statim dixit, Non omnes cápiunt, sed quibus datum est? Ut singuláre id esse certámen perdíscas, non ut sorte datam necessitátem suspicéris.

Quibus motus Parisiénsis Antístes, ad sacrum Presbyterátus órdinem præ humilitáte reluctántem promóvit, eo consílio, ut in ea civitáte cómmorans, sapiéntia et móribus studiósæ juventúti prælucéret. <c>S</c>ic stabilíto Ordine, sancti Fundatóres in Gálliam rediérunt; primóque cœnóbio Cervi Frígidi in diœcési Meldénsi constrúcto, ad ejus régimen Felix remánsit, et Joánnes Romam cum áliquot sóciis revérsus est, ubi Innocéntius domum, ecclésiam, et hospitále sancti Thomæ de Formis in monte Cœlio eis donávit, cum multis redítibus et possessiónibus. Datis quoque lítteris ad Miramolínum regem Maróchii, opus redemptiónis felíci auspício inchoátum fuit. Tum ad Hispánias, sub jugo Saracenórum magna ex parte oppréssas, Joánnes proféctus est; regúmque, príncipum, atque aliórum fidélium ánimos ad captivórum et páuperum commiseratiónem commóvit. Monastéria ædificávit, hospitália eréxit, magnóque lucro animárum plures captívos redémit. Romam tandem revérsus, sanctísque opéribus incúmbens, assíduis labóribus attrítus, et morbo conféctus, ardentíssimo Dei et próximi amóre exæstuans, ad extrémum devénit. Quare frátribus convocátis, eísque ad opus redemptiónis cælitus præmonstrátum efficáciter cohortátis, obdormívit in Dómino, sextodécimo Kaléndas Januárii, anno salútis millésimo ducentésimo décimo tértio, ejúsque corpus in ipsa ecclésia sancti Thomæ de Formis condígno honóre tumulátum fuit.

<c>B</c>ernárdus Cátanæ in Sicília ex família de Scámmacca, sánguine et pietáte illústri, ortum hábuit. Adoléscens sæculi illécebris tractus, cupiditátibus laxátas habénas dedit. Cum vero in omni vanitátis et lubricitátis cœno plane cæcus agerétur et præceps, ineffábilis in eum respéxit divína misericórdia: nam gravi afféctus vúlnere, dum prostrátum a vítiis desístere felix compellébat necéssitas, ætérnæ suæ salútis perículum, supérno coruscánte lúmine, agnóvit, atque ut melióra de se ágeret obtínuit. Mundum ítaque, cujus technas calamitatésque expértus fúerat, desérere et contémnere státuit. Prístinæ restitútus sanitáti, quod decréverat, in Prædicatórum Ordine perficiéndum curávit. Ad convéntum ítaque sancti Domínici véniens, a Præsule, ut in eórum consórtium admitterétur, eníxis précibus postulávit, quod ei pro votis cessit.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<c>C</c>ándida in Prædicatórum família redimítus veste, simul visus est novum induísse hóminem. Etenim in obediéntia, humilitáte, mansuetúdine, ac modéstia, aliísque virtútibus, perfectióres æmulándo, máxime præstábat. Sério perpéndens Institúti, in quo fuit cooptátus, præcípuum onus esse aliórum salúti inténdere, sublevándis proximórum necessitátibus ímpigre occurrébat: quod ut efficácius præstáret, Deum prophetíæ dono illum exornásse perhibétur. Ne autem dum áliis prædicáret, réprobus ipse efficerétur, utque juventútis crímina pœniténtiæ labóribus deléret, diris sese cruentábat flagéllis, ac vitam in summa asperitáte ducébat. Caritáte exæstuans in Deum, ita in rerum divinárum contemplatióne assídue detinebátur, ut sæpe divína passus fúerit: in quibus aliquándo toto córpore a terra elevátum, quandóque vero supérno circumfúsum lúmine illum fratres aspexére, ut vétera monuménta ferunt.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<c>T</c>andem post vitam in exactíssima legum sui Institúti observántia transáctam, ad Súperos, ut repósitam opéribus justítiæ corónam accíperet, anno millésimo quadringentésimo octogésimo sexto felíciter evolávit. Ejus tránsitus pervulgáta fama, magnus ad ejus corpus, venerándi causa, factus est cívium concúrsus. Alíquibus transáctis annis, de ipsíus córporis in decentiórem locum translatióne actum fuit: quod quidem fervéntius ac devótius complétum est, cum íntegrum, sicut etiámnum appáret, fúerit repértum. Multis in vita et post mortem miráculis claruísse tráditur. Cultum vero religiósum ab ejus óbitu eídem constánter tribútum, et ad hæc usque témpora nunquam intermíssum, Leo Duodécimus Póntifex Máximus ex sacræ Rítuum Congregatiónis consúlto probávit, et ut in univérso Prædicatórum Ordine, ac civitáte et diœcési Catanénsi de beáto Bernárdo Offícium recitári, ac Missa celebrári possit, benígne concéssit.

<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>C</c>hriste, qui lux es et dies,
Noctis tenébras détegis,
Lucísque lumen créderis,
Lumen beátum prǽdicans.

<h>P</h>recámur sancte Dómine,
defénde nos in hac nocte:
Sit nobis in te réquies,
Quiétam noctem tríbue.

<h>N</h>e gravis somnus írruat,
Nec hostis nos subrípiat,
Nec caro illi conséntiens
Nos tibi reos státuat.

<h>O</h>culi somnum cápiant,
Cor ad te semper vígilet:
Déxtera tua prótegat
Fámulos, qui te díligunt.

Insidiántes réprime,
Gubérna tuos fámulos,
<n>Ad hunc Vers. genuflectatur</n>
Quos Sánguine mercátus es.

<h>M</h>eménto nostri, Dómine,
In gravi isto córpore:
Qui es defénsor ánimæ,
Adésto nobis, Dómine.

<h>P</h>ræsta Pater omnípotens,
Per Jesum Christum Dóminum,
Qui tecum in perpétuum
Regnat cum Sancto Spíritu.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Custódi nos, Dómine, ut pupíllam óculi.

defénde nos in hac nocte:

Govern thy servants,

<c>Q</c>uis mihi det te fratrem meum sugéntem úbera matris meæ, ut invéniam te foris, et deósculer te, et jam me nemo despíciat? Apprehéndam te, et ducam in domum matris meæ: ibi me docébis, et dabo tibi póculum ex vino condíto, et mustum malórum granatórum meórum. Læva ejus sub cápite meo, et déxtera illíus amplexábitur me. Adjúro vos fíliæ Jerúsalem, ne suscitétis, neque evigiláre faciátis diléctam donec ipsa velit.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<c>C</c>aritáte in Deum fervens, oratióni fere assídue vacábat, quidquid témporis necessáriis occupatiónibus et módicæ quiéti supérerat, in ea insúmens: utque corpus in servitútem redígeret, férrea caténa et flagéllis illud macerábat. Cibi parcíssima, octo supra quadragínta annis cárnibus abstínuit, legumínibus plerúmque et herbis vescens, intérdum vero solo pane et aqua conténta. Proximórum ætérnam salútem exóptans, ardentíssimas ad Deum pro peccatórum conversióne preces fundébat. Tanto étiam commiseratiónis sensu erga purgántem ánimam commóta est, ut acerbíssimos dolóres, sibi divínitus inflíctos, in pœnárum illi debitárum expiatiónem pertulísse visa sit. Exímia prudéntia et reguláris observántiæ zelo moniáles diu rexit, eas non minus exémplo quam adhortatiónibus ad omnem sanctimóniam infórmans: quo in offício humilitátem ádeo cóluit, ut abjectíssima quæque ópera sponte obíret, ac infírmis præcípua caritáte et summo stúdio inservíret.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Lectio vi</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Ignem sui amóris accéndat Deus in córdibus nostris.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>S</c>upernórum charísmatum cópia singuláris in ea enítuit, ánulo desponsatiónis, sacrísque stigmátibus, quæ non semel spectánda se exhibuérunt, accéptis. Plúrium annórum spátio, quinta et sexta Féria in altíssimam contemplatiónem rapta, síngulos Redemptóris cruciátus in Passióne tolerátos ex órdine in córpore mirabíliter sentíre consuévit. Prati degens, sanctum Philíppum Nérium, Romæ commorántem, vidére proméruit, ejúsque collóquio frui. Extasum, ráptuum, cæléstium visiónum, ac prophétici lúminis dono illústris, futúra prædíxit, ac simul occúlta revelávit. Grávibus dénique morbis decúmbens, Ecclésiæ Sacraméntis muníta, anno a Christo nato millésimo quingentésimo nonagésimo, ætátis sexagésimo nono, quarto Nonas Februárii in cælum migrávit. Eam Benedíctus Décimus quartus Póntifex Máximus solémni ritu sanctárum Vírginum fastis adscrípsit, anno salútis millésimo septingentésimo quadragésimo sexto.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℣.</r> Ego autem exsultábo, et gaudébo in Deo Jesu meo. Ténui eum, nec dimíttam.

<h>Lectio vii</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Evangélica léctio sit nobis salus et protéctio.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>I</c>n illo témpore: Dixit Jesus discípulis suis parábolam hanc: Simile erit regnum cælórum decem virgínibus: quæ accipiéntes lámpades suas exiérunt óbviam sponso, et sponsæ. Et réliqua.
<r>Homilía sancti Augustíni Epíscopi.</r>
<c>I</c>ntelligámus, caríssimi, ad omnes nos, id est ad univérsam omníno Ecclésiam pertinére istam parábolam. Quare ergo quinque, et quinque vírgines? Istæ quinque, et quinque vírgines. omnes omníno sunt ánimæ Christianórum, non qualescúmque ánimæ, sed tales ánimæ, quæ habent cathólicam fidem, et habére vidéntur bona ópera in Ecclésia Dei: et tamen ex ipsis quinque sunt prudéntes, et quinque fátuæ. Quare ergo appellátæ sunt quinque, et quare vírgines, prius videámus: et deínde cétera considerémus. Omnis ánima in córpore ídeo quinário número censétur, quia quinque sénsibus útitur. Qui ergo se ábstinet ab illícito visu, ab illícito audítu, ab illícito odorátu, ab illícito gustátu, ab illícito tactu, propter ipsam integritátem, Vírginis nomen accépit.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Responsorium vii</h>
<r>℟.</r> Mihi absit gloriári nisi in Cruce Dómini nostri Jesu Christi: * Per quem mihi mundus crucifíxus est, et ego mundo.
<r>℣.</r> Sicut abúndant passiónes Christi in nobis, ita et per Christum abúndat consolátio nostra. Per quem mihi.

<r>Benedictio.</r> Divínum auxílium máneat semper nobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>S</c>ed si bonum est abstinére ab illícitis sentiéndi mótibus, et ídeo unaquǽque ánima christiána Vírginis nomen accépit, quare quinque admittúntur, et quinque repellúntur? Et vírgines sunt, et repellúntur. Parum est, quia vírgines sunt, et lámpades habent. Vírgines propter abstinéntiam ab illícitis sénsibus, lámpades habent propter ópera bona; de quibus opéribus Dóminus dicit: Lúceant ópera vestra coram homínibus, ut vídeant bona facta vestra, et gloríficent Patrem vestrum, qui in cælis est. Item discípulis dicit: Sint lumbi vestri præcíncti, et lucérnæ ardéntes. In lumbis accínctis virgínitas, in lucérnis ardéntibus ópera bona.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.

c44caf5342:
<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Apoc. 19</r>
<c>R</c>egnávit Dóminus Deus noster omnípotens: gaudeámus, et exsultémus: et demus glóriam ei: quia venérunt núptiæ Agni, et uxor ejus præparávit se.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>I</c>esu, coróna Vírginum,
Quem Mater illa cóncipit
Quæ sola Virgo párturit,
Hæc vota clemens áccipe:

<h>Q</h>ui pascis inter lília
Septus choréis Vírginum,
Sponsus decórus glória
Sponsísque reddens prǽmia.

<h>Q</h>uocúmque pergis, Vírgines
Sequúntur, atque láudibus
Post te canéntes cúrsitant,
Hymnósque dulces pérsonant;

<h>T</h>e deprecámur lárgius,
Nostris adáuge sénsibus
Nescíre prorsus ómnia
Corruptiónis vúlnera.

<h>L</h>aus, honor, virtus, glória
Deo Patri et Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
In sæculórum sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Adducéntur regi vírgines post eam.
<r>℟.</r> Próximæ ejus afferéntur tibi.
33f78d40bf:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Apoc. 19</r>
<c>R</c>egnávit Dóminus Deus noster omnípotens: gaudeámus, et exsultémus: et demus glóriam ei: quia venérunt núptiæ Agni, et uxor ejus præparávit se.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>J</c>esu, the virgins' crown, do thou
Accept us as in prayer we bow;
Born of that Virgin, whom alone
The mother and the maid we own.

<h>A</h>mongst the lilies thou dost feed,
By virgin choirs accompanied;
With glory decked, the spotless brides
Whose bridal gifts thy love provides.

<h>T</h>hey, wheresoe'er thy footsteps bend,
With hymns and praises still attend:
In blessèd troops they follow thee,
With dance, and song, and melody.

<h>W</h>e pray thee therefore to bestow
Upon our senses here below
Thy grace, that so we may endure
From taint of all corruption pure.

<h>A</h>ll laud to God the Father be,
All praise, eternal Son, to thee;
All glory as is ever meet,
To God, the holy Paraclete.
Amen.

e031ad0334:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>S</c>ummi largítor prǽmii,
Spes qui es única mundi,
Preces inténde servórum,
Ad te devóte clamántium.

<h>N</h>ostra te consciéntia
Grave offendísse monstra:
Quam emúndes, supplicámus,
Ab ómnibus piáculis.

<h>S</h>i rénuis, quis tríbuet?
Indúlge, quia potens es:
Te corde rogáre mundo
Fac nos precámur, Dómine.

<h>E</h>rgo nunc accépta nostrum,
Qui sacrásti jejúnium:
Quo mýstice paschália
Capiámus sacraménta.

<h>S</h>umma nobis hoc cónferat
In Deitáte Trínitas:
In qua gloriátur unus
Per cuncta sǽcula Deus.
Amen.
e6c3bd05ee:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>T</c>he fast, as taught by holy lore,
We keep in solemn course once more:
The fast to all men known, and bound
In forty days of yearly round.

<h>T</h>he law and seers that were of old
In diverse ways this Lent foretold,
Which Christ, all seasons’ King and Guide,
In after ages sanctified.

<h>M</h>ore sparing therefore let us make
The words we speak, the food we take,
Our sleep and mirth, —and closer barred
Be every sense in holy guard.

<h>A</h>void the evil thoughts that roll
Like waters o’er the heedless soul;
Nor let the foe occasion find
Our souls in slavery to bind.

<h>I</h>n prayer together let us fall,
And cry for mercy, one and all,
And weep before the Judge’s feet,
And his avenging wrath entreat.

<h>T</h>hy grace have we offended sore,
By sins, O God, which we deplore;
But pour upon us from on high,
O pardoning One, thy clemency.

<h>R</h>emember thou, though frail we be,
That yet thine handiwork are we;
Nor let the honour of thy name
Be by another put to shame.

<h>F</h>orgive the sin that we have wrought;
Increase the good that we have sought:
That we at length, our wanderings o'er,
May please thee here and evermore.

<h>G</h>rant O thou Blessed Trinity,
Grant, O Essential Unity,
That this our fast of forty days
May work our profit and thy praise.
Amen.

a3b7660e30:
<h>Lectio iv</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Deus Pater omnípotens sit nobis propítius et clemens.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>J</c>ordánus in óppido Botérgæ provínciæ Saxóniæ ex illústri família ducum Ebernstein oríginem duxit. Adhuc in sǽculo exsístens, pietátem sibi pleníssime vindicávit. Erat enim super míseros pia gestans víscera, ita ut raro vel nunquam pauper ab eo sine eleemósyna discéderet: et cum aliquándo peténti nihil habéret quod daret, cíngulum concéssit. Ecclésiam deínde oratúrus ingréssus, Crucifíxum vidit illo præcínctum: cujus spectáculo plúrimum commótus, togam Religiónis assúmere constítuit. Quare mundo valedícens, a Regináldo viro óptimo in Prædicatórum Órdinem recéptus fuit. Ibi lenis ac mitis appáruit, cibi somníque parcíssimus: humilitátis servándæ stúdio honóres oblátos sapiénter declinávit. Ab oratiónis assuéto exercítio nulla re deflécti pótuit, et meditatiónibus, ex quibus miram eliciébat suavitátem, totus et ubíque incumbébat.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Responsorium iv</h>
<r>℟.</r> Magnificávit eum in conspéctu regum, * Et dedit illi corónam glóriæ.
<r>℣.</r> Státuit illi testaméntum sempitérnum, et beatificávit illum in glória. Et dedit illi.

92fe180b6f:
<h>Lectio v</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Ad gáudia paradísi perdúcat nos misericórdia Christi.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>D</c>efúncto sancto Patre Domínico, propter magnam in vita et doctrína probitátem dignus hábitus est ut ei sufficerétur: et quia zelo salútis animárum máxime afficiebátur, in regímine pósitus nihil intentátum relíquit, unde Ordo látius amplificarétur. Licet multis magnísque curis occupátus, nunquam tamen a verbi Dei prædicatióne déstitit. Delinquéntes, ubi oportéret, sevére corrigébat, sed tali ac tanta utebátur grátia, ut humanitáte pótius quam severitáte illos devínceret. Sicut corporális vita cibi potúsque mútua commistióne sustinétur, ita oratiónis studiorúmque Scripturárum altérnas exercitatiónes pro vitæ spirituális increménto adhibéndas esse docébat: ac ut uberióres in oratióne eliceréntur fructus, in eo insisténdum, ubi major haberétur devótio. Erga beatíssimam Vírginem devotíssimus fuit, modúmque eam fervéntius deprecándi áliis tríbuit, ac ut post Completórium Salve Regína canerétur primus dispósuit. Céterum tantæ fuit virtútis, ut áltero captus óculo, secum fratres congaudéndi causa vocáverit, ceu ab inimíco liberátus.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Responsorium v</h>
<r>℟.</r> Amávit eum Dóminus, et ornávit eum: stolam glóriæ índuit eum, * Et ad portas paradísi coronávit eum.

<r>Benedictio.</r> Ignem sui amóris accéndat Deus in córdibus nostris.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>T</c>andem ánimo constítuit Hierosólymam, viséndi grátia sacra Redemptiónis nostræ loca ac fratrum cœnóbia, pétere: sed cum prope Achon pervenísset, ingénti obórta tempestáte, cum duóbus sóciis, fracta navi, in flúctibus périit, et ita ab hoc sǽculo nequam eréptus est. Ejus córpori ad litus ejécto lúmina de cælo delápsa noctu insedísse, nimiúmque odórem sepeliéntium mánibus per plures dies adhæsísse memóriæ tráditum est. Servi sui glóriam Deus sanctæ Lutgárdæ aliísque maniféste osténdit. Nam magna luce æque ac cruce insignítus appárens, dixit: Exívi de hoc sǽculo ad glóriam Beatórum, et inter Apostolórum choros et Prophetárum evéctus sum. Multis magnísque claruísse miráculis sanctus Antonínus aliíque auctóres gravíssimi fidem fáciunt: unde religiósum cultum proméruit, quem multíplici monumentórum génere ad nostra usque témpora probátum, Leo Duodécimus Póntifex Máximus ex sacræ Rítuum Congregatiónis consúlto confirmávit, utque de beáto Jordáno in univérso Prædicatórum Ordine Offícium recitári ac Missa celebrári possit indúlsit.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<c>G</c>regórius Décimus, Theáldus seu Theobáldus ántea nuncupátus, Placéntiæ ad Æmiliæ fines nóbili Vicecómitum génere natus est. Adoléscens ecclesiásticæ milítiæ adscríptus, singulári nítuit honestáte morum vitæque mundítia, nulla unquam, ut créditur, críminis contagióne pollúta. In Gálliam cum Jacóbo Cardináli Pecorário Gregórii Noni Legáto proféctus, Archidiáconus Leodiénsis renuntiátus est. Eo in Itáliam redeúnte, theologíæ Parísiis óperam dedit, ac magístri munus adéptus, verbo et exémplo fidéles ac príncipes ad Terræ sanctæ recuperatiónem veheménter accéndit. In Syriam deínde peregrinátus, dum ibi sacram expeditiónem urgéret, a Cardinálibus, Vitérbii Pontíficis electiónem in annum fere tértium protrahéntibus, in Petri Sedem evéctus est anno millésimo ducentésimo septuagésimo primo.

<c>A</c>ccépto Ptolemáide electiónis decréto, in Itáliam navigávit, ac Vitérbium se cóntulit, deínde Romam: ubi anno insequénte solémniter inaugurátus est. Ab ipso Pontificátus exórdio, ad generális concílii celebratiónem curas et cogitatiónes omnes adjécit. Eo Lugdúnum Galliárum indícto, Michaélem Palæólogum Græcórum imperatórem, tum álios christiános príncipes et Græcæ Latinæque Ecclésiæ præsules lítteris amantíssimis invitávit: arcessítis étiam exímiis doctrína et sanctitáte viris, uti sancto Thoma Aquináte, in ipso itínere vita functo, sancto Bonaventúra, sancto Philíppo Benítio, beáto Albérto Magno, Petro de Tarantásia Ordinis Prædicatórum, qui eídem in Pontificátu succéssit. Igitur œcuménicam synodum, Patrum número ómnium frequentíssimam, cui præfuit Póntifex ipse, Græcis ejuráto schísmate ad Ecclésiæ unitátem recéptis, decrétis pro sacra expeditióne subsídiis, editísque plúribus sanctíssimis légibus, triméstri spátio felíciter celebrávit.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.

<c>D</c>e pace in Ecclésia firmánda cumprímis sollícitus, prælatórum dissídia, regum inimicítias, provinciárum ódia, populórum factiónes compósuit, dirémit, exstínxit. Ecclésiæ jura, étiam advérsus reges et príncipes, sevére ac fórtiter vindicávit: nullam esse prædicans solidiórem regnórum basim quam tutélam ecclesiásticæ libertátis. Páuperum amantíssimus, primus ómnium in Apostólico palátio piárum in illos largitiónum præsidem constítuit, iísque própriis mánibus pedes quotídie abluébat. In Itáliam a concílio redux, dum profectiónem in Palæstínam meditátur, plúraque ália christiánæ reipúblicæ bono molirétur, Arétii in Etrúria morte intercéptus est, quarto ab electióne sua anno, mense quarto, die décima. Fuit vir ánimi plane invícti et apostólici, terrenórum contémptu, cultus divíni stúdio, fídei zelo, disciplínæ et morum restauratióne, rerum gerendárum prudéntia, fortitúdine, magnanimitáte, aliísque virtútibus prorsus exímius. Miráculis post mortem claruísse, Ecclésiæ Aretínæ monuménta testántur.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

Erst on this feast-day merited to enter

Now and forever.

Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.

<c>A</c>lvarus Cordubénsis, avítæ géneris claritáti exímiæ sanctitátis decus adjúnxit. Nam a prima adolescéntia, posthábitis terrénis ómnibus, Prædicatórum Ordini nomen dedit, in quo spíritu et lítteris mirífice profécit. Absolúto studiórum cursu, prædicatióni se totum impéndit, ac plures Hispániæ nec non Itáliæ partes ubérrimo animárum fructu evangelizándo peragrávit. Joánni Secúndo Castéllæ regi ejúsque matri Catharínæ a confessiónibus fuit: sed religiósæ solitúdinis stúdio, dimissióne petíta, ab aula secéssit, ac régia ope novum Ordinis cœnóbium sub appellatióne sancti Domínici Scalæ cæli, prope Córdubam, a fundaméntis excitávit: ubi cum áliis sui Ordinis frátribus severiórem colens disciplínam, vitam sanctíssimam duxit.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<c>C</c>órpori suo, velut hosti nondum subácto, bellum perpétuum omni asperitátum afflictationúmque génere íntulit. Noctes ante divíni Sacraménti altáre fere ducébat insómnes, non áliam quandóque fesso córpori quiétem indúlgens quam brevem ádmodum, lápidi inníxus, vel altári. Páuperum ac miserórum ómnium ærúmnis veheménter compátiens, quamcúmque posset opem amantíssime ferébat. Obvium sibi aliquándo páuperem toto córpore ulcerósum, própria involútum cappa, humerísque superimpósitum ad cœnóbium détulit, curam ejus actúrus. The deep meaning is given; but what is considered is the lie because men do not understand the way in which that signification, which is a truth, is set forth but the falsehood is plainly expressed, and believed. That we may understand this more plainly by taking some points in illustration, consider with me what Jacob did. It is certain that he covered his limbs with the skins of goats. If we consider his object in point of fact, we shall find that it was to lie, because he did this that he might be thought to be he who he was not. But if we consider this his deed in that deep typical sense which it undoubtedly possesseth, we find that by the goat-skins are represented sins, and by him who covered himself therewith Him Who bore not His own sins, but the sins of others.

<h>Lectio iv</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Deus Pater omnípotens sit nobis propítius et clemens.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>P</c>etrus Ravénnæ honéstis paréntibus natus, adhuc lactens a matre numerósæ prolis pertæsa abjícitur: sed domésticæ mulíeris ópera semivívus excéptus ac recreátus, genitríci ad humanitátis sensum revocátæ rédditur. Utróque orbátus parénte, tamquam vile mancípium sub áspera fratris tutéla duram servitútem exércuit. Religiónis in Deum ac pietátis erga patrem, egrégium tunc spécimen dedit: invéntum síquidem forte nummum, non própriæ inédiæ sublevándæ, sed Sacerdóti, qui divínum Sacrifícium ad illíus expiatiónem offérret, erogávit. A Damiáno fratre, a quo, uti fertur, cognoméntum accépit, benígne recéptus, ejus cura lítteris erudítur, in quibus brevi tantum profécit, ut magístris admiratióni esset. Cum autem liberálibus sciéntiis floréret et nómine, eas cum laude dócuit. Interim, ut corpus ratióni súbderet, sub móllibus véstibus cilícium adhíbuit, jejúniis, vigíliis et oratiónibus solérter insístens. Calénte juvénta dum carnis stímulis ácriter urgerétur, insultántium libídinum faces rigéntibus flúvii mersus aquis noctu exstinguébat; tum venerabília quæque loca obíre, totúmque Psaltérium recitáre consuéverat. Ope assídua páuperes levábat, quibus frequénter pastis convívio própriis ipse mánibus ministrábat.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Responsorium iv</h>

<r>℣.</r> Státuit illi testaméntum sempitérnum, et beatificávit illum in glória. Et dedit illi.

<h>Lectio v</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Ad gáudia paradísi perdúcat nos misericórdia Christi.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>P</c>erficiéndæ magis vitæ causa, in Avellanénsi Eugubínæ diœcésis cœnóbio Ordini monachórum sanctæ Crucis Fontis Avellánæ, a beáto Lodúlpho, sancti Romuáldi discípulo, fundáto, nomen dedit. Non ita multo post, in monastérium Pomposiánum, mox in cœnóbium sancti Vincéntii Petræ Pertúsæ ab Abbáte suo missus, utrúmque ascetérium verbo sacro, præcláris institutiónibus et móribus excóluit. Ad suos revocátus, post Præsidis óbitum, Avellanitárum famíliæ præfícitur, quam novis, váriis in locis, exstrúctis domicíliis et sanctíssimis institútis ita auxit, ut alter ejus Ordinis Parens, ac præcípuum ornaméntum jure sit hábitus. Salutárem Petri sollicitúdinem ália quoque divérsi institúti cœnóbia, Canonicórum convéntus, et pópuli sunt expérti. Urbináti diœcési non uno nómine prófuit. Theuzóni Epíscopo in causa gravíssima assédit, ipsúmque in recte administrándo episcopátu consílio et ópera juvit. Divinórum contemplatióne, córporis maceratiónibus, ceterísque spectátæ sanctimóniæ exémplis excélluit. His motus Stéphanus Nonus Póntifex Máximus eum licet invítum et reluctántem sanctæ Románæ Ecclésiæ Cardinálem creávit, et Ostiénsem Epíscopum. Quas Petrus dignitátes splendidíssimis virtútibus et consentáneis episcopáli ministério opéribus gessit.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Amávit eum Dóminus, et ornávit eum: stolam glóriæ índuit eum, * Et ad portas paradísi coronávit eum.
<r>℣.</r> Índuit eum Dóminus lorícam fídei, et ornávit eum. Et ad portas.

<h>Lectio vi</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Ignem sui amóris accéndat Deus in córdibus nostris.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>D</c>ifficíllimo témpore Románæ Ecclésiæ Summísque Pontifícibus doctrína, legatiónibus aliísque suscéptis labóribus mirífice ádfuit. Advérsus Nicolaitárum et Simoníacam hæreses ad mortem usque strénue decertávit. Hujúsmodi depúlsis malis, Mediolanénsem Ecclésiæ Románæ conciliávit. Benedícto et Cadalóo falsis Pontifícibus fórtiter réstitit. Henrícum Quartum Germániæ regem ab iníquo uxóris divórtio detérruit. Ravennátes ad débita Románo Pontífici obséquia revocátos sacris restítuit. Canónicos Velitérnos ad sanctióris vitæ leges compósuit. In província præsértim Urbináte vix ulla fuit episcopális Ecclésia, de qua Petrus non sit beneméritus: Eugubínam, quam aliquándo créditam hábuit, multis levávit incómmodis: álias álibi, quando opórtuit, perínde curávit, ac si suæ essent tutélæ commíssæ. Cardinalátu et episcopáli dignitáte depósitis, nihil de prístina juvándi próximos sedulitáte remísit. Jejúnium sextæ Fériæ in honórem sanctæ Crucis Jesu Christi: horárias beátæ Dei Genitrícis preces ejúsque die Sábbato cultum propagávit. Inferéndæ quoque sibi verberatiónis morem ad patratórum scélerum expiatiónem provéxit. Demum sanctitáte, doctrína, miráculis et præcláre actis illústris, dum e Ravennáte legatióne redíret, Favéntiæ octávo Kaléndas Mártii migrávit ad Christum. Ejus corpus ibídem apud Cisterciénses multis miráculis clarum, frequénti populórum veneratióne cólitur. Ipsum Faventíni non semel in præsénti discrímine propítium expérti, Patrónum apud Deum delegérunt. Leo vero Duodécimus Póntifex Máximus Offícium Missámque in ejus honórem tamquam Confessóris Pontíficis, quæ alíquibus in diœcésibus atque in Ordine Camaldulénsium jam celebrabántur, ex sacrórum Rítuum Congregatiónis consúlto, áddita Doctóris qualitáte, ad univérsam exténdit Ecclésiam.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Responsorium vi</h>
<r>℟.</r> Sancte Petre Christi Conféssor, audi rogántes sérvulos, * Et impetrátam cǽlitus Tu defer indulgéntiam.
<r>℣.</r> O sancte Petre, sidus áureum, Dómini grátia, servórum gémitus sólita súscipe cleméntia. Et impetrátam.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Tu defer indulgéntiam.

<c>S</c>cholástica venerábilis Patris Benedícti soror, omnipoténti Dómino ab ipso infántiæ témpore dedicáta, ad eum semel per annum veníre consuéverat, ad quam Vir Dei non longe extra jánuam in possessióne monastérii descendébat. Quadam vero die venit ex more, atque ad eam cum discípulis venerábilis ejus descéndit frater: qui totum diem in Dei láudibus, sacrísque collóquiis ducéntes, incumbéntibus jam noctis ténebris, simul accepérunt cibum. Cumque adhuc ad mensam sedérent, et inter sacra collóquia tárdior se hora protráheret, éadem sanctimoniális fémina, soror ejus, eum rogávit, dicens: Quæso te, ut ista nocte me non déseras, ut usque mane de cæléstis vitæ gáudiis loquámur. Cui ille respóndit: Quid est, quod lóqueris soror? Manére extra cellam nullátenus possum. Tanta vero erat cæli serénitas, ut nulla in áere nubes apparéret. Sanctimoniális autem fémina, cum verba fratris negántis audivísset, insértas dígitis manus super mensam pósuit, et caput in mánibus, omnipoténtem Dóminum rogatúra, declinávit. Cumque leváret de mensa caput, tanta coruscatiónis et tonítrui virtus, tántaque inundátio plúviæ erúpit, ut neque venerábilis Benedíctus, neque fratres, qui cum eo áderant, extra loci limen, quo conséderant, pedem movére potúerint.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<c>I</c>ste Conféssor Dómini sacrátus,

Scándere cæli.

Vita dum præsens vegetávit ejus
Córporis artus.

Membra languéntum modo sanitáti,
Quólibet morbo fúerint graváta,
Restituúntur.

Ipsius, hymnum canit hunc libénter:

Omne per ævum.

<c>T</c>his the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

<h>S</h>aintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

<h>S</h>ick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.

Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.

Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

That in his merits we may have a portion,

2b7230db6c:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>P</c>ange, lingua, gloriósi
Prœlium certáminis,
Et super Crucis trophǽo
Dic triúmphum nóbilem,
Quáliter Redémptor orbis
Immolátus vícerit.

<h>D</h>e paréntis protoplásti
Fraude Factor cóndolens,
Quando pomi noxiális
Morsu in mortem córruit,
Ipse lignum tunc notávit,
Damna ligni ut sólveret.

<h>H</h>oc opus nostræ salútis
Ordo depopóscerat,
Multifórmis proditóris
Ars ut artem fálleret,
Et medélam ferret inde,
Hostis unde lǽserat.

<h>Q</h>uando venit ergo sacri
Plenitúdo témporis,
Missus est ab arce Patris
Natus, orbis Cónditor,
Atque ventre virgináli
Carne amíctus pródiit.

<h>V</h>agit infans inter arcta
Cónditus præsépia:
Membra pannis involúta
Virgo Mater álligat:
Et manus, pedésque, et crura
Stricta cingit fáscia.

<h>G</h>lória, et honor Deo
Usqueqáque Altíssimo,
Una Patri, Filióque;
Inclyto Paráclito:
Cui laus est et potéstas,
Per ætérna sǽcula.
Amen.
58ff6dd241:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>S</c>ing, my tongue, the glorious battle
Sing the last, the dread affray;
O'er the cross, the victor's trophy,
Sound the high triumphal lay:
Tell how Christ, the world's Redeemer,
As a victim won the day.

<h>G</h>od, his Maker, sorely grieving
That the first-made Adam fell,
When he ate the fruit of sorrow,
Whose reward was death and hell,
Noted then this wood, the ruin
Of the ancient wood to quell.

<h>F</h>or the work of our salvation
Needs would have his order so,
And the multiform deceiver's
Art by art would overthrow,
And from thence would bring the med'cine
Whence the insult of the foe.

<h>W</h>herefore, when the sacred fullness
Of the appointed time was come,
This world's Maker left his Father,
Sent the heav'nly mansion from,
And proceeded, God Incarnate,
Of the Virgin's holy womb.

<h>W</h>eeps the infant in the manger
That in Bethlehem's stable stands;
And his limbs the Virgin Mother
Doth compose in swaddling bands,
Meetly thus in linen folding
Of her God the feet and hands.

<h>T</h>o the Trinity be glory
Everlasting, as is meet;
Equal to the Father, equal
To the Son, and Paraclete:
Trinal Unity, whose praises
All created things repeat.
Amen.

Penset ergo apud se unusquísque vestrum, si hæc vox Dei in cordis ejus aure conváluit, et quia jam ex Deo sit, agnóscit. Nam sunt nonnúlli, qui præcépta Dei nec aure córporis percípere dignántur. <h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Jer 11</r>
<c>T</c>u autem, Dómine Sábaoth, qui júdicas juste, et probas renes et corda, vídeam ultiónem tuam ex eis: tibi enim revelávi causam meam, Dómine Deus meus.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>L</c>ustris sex qui jam peráctis,
Tempus implens córporis,
Se volénte natus ad hoc,
Passióni déditus,
Agnus in Crucis levátur
Immolándus stípite.

<h>H</h>ic acétum, fel, arúndo,
Sputa, clavi, láncea:
Mite corpus perforátur,
Sanguis, unda prófluit:
Terra, pontus, astra, mundus,
Quo lavántur flúmine!

<h>C</h>rux fidélis, inter omnes
Arbor una nóbilis:
Nulla silva talem profert
Fronde, flore, gérmine:
Dulce lignum, dulces clavos,
Dulce pondus sústinet.

<h>F</h>lecte ramos, arbor alta,
Tensa laxa víscera,
Et rigor lentéscat ille,
Quem dedit natívitas:
Ut supérni membra Regis
Miti tendas stípite.

<h>S</h>ola digna tu fuísti
Ferre sæcli prétium,
Atque portum præparáre
Nauta mundo náufrago,
Quem sacer cruor perúnxit,
Fusus Agni córpore.

<h>G</h>lória et honor Deo
Usquequáque altíssimo:
Una Patri, Filióque,
Inclyto Paráclito:
Cui laus est et potéstas
Per ætérna sǽcula.
Amen.

<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Jer 11</r>
<c>B</c>ut thou, O Lord of Sabaoth, who judgest justly, and triest the reins and hearts, let me see thy revenge on them: for to thee I have revealed my cause, O Lord my God.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>T</c>hirty years among us dwelling,
His appointed time fulfilled,
Born for this, he meets his passion,
For that this he freely willed:
On the cross the Lamb is lifted,
Where his life-blood shall be spilled.

<h>H</h>e endured the nails, the spitting,
Vinegar, and spear, and reed;
From that holy body broken
Blood and water forth proceed:
Earth, and stars, and sky, and ocean,
By that flood from stain are free.

<h>F</h>aithful cross! above all other,
One and only noble tree!
None in foliage, none in blossom,
None in fruit thy peers may be;
Sweetest wood and sweetest iron!
Sweetest weight is hung on thee.

<h>B</h>end thy boughs, O tree of glory!
Thy relaxing sinews bend;
For awhile the ancient rigour,
That thy birth bestowed, suspend;
And the King of heavenly beauty
On thy bosom gently tend!

<h>T</h>hou alone wast counted worthy
This world's ransom to uphold;
For a shipwrecked race preparing
Harbour, like the ark of old;
With the sacred blood anointed
From the smitten Lamb that rolled.

<h>T</h>o the Trinity be glory
Everlasting, as is meet;
Equal to the Father, equal
To the Son, and Paraclete:
Trinal Unity, whose praises
All created things repeat.
Amen.

<r>℟.</r> And defend me from them that rise up against me.

<r>Jer 12:4-7</r>
How long shall the land mourn, and the herb of every field wither for the wickedness of them that dwell therein? The beasts and the birds are consumed: because they have said: He shall not see our last end. If thou hast wearied with running with footmen, how canst thou contend with horses? and if thou hast been secure in a land of peace, what wilt thou do in the swelling of the Jordan? For even thy brethren, and the house of thy father, even they have fought against thee, and have cried after thee with full voice: believe them not when they speak good things to thee. I have forsaken my house, I have left my inheritance: I have given my dear soul into the land of her enemies.
Thus saith the Lord God: Be converted to me, and you shall be saved.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<c>R</c>elíqui domum meam, dimísi hereditátem meam: dedi diléctam ánimam meam in manu inimicórum ejus. Facta est mihi heréditas mea quasi leo in silva: dedit contra me vocem, ídeo odívi eam. I have forsaken my house, I have left my inheritance: I have given my dear soul into the land of her enemies. 137ebfa409:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>A</c>uróra lucis rútilat,
Cælum láudibus íntonat,
Mundus exsúltans iúbilat,
Gemens inférnus úlulat:

<h>C</h>um Rex ille fortíssimus,
Mortis confráctis víribus,
Pede concúlcans tártara,
Solvit a pœna míseros.

<h>I</h>lle qui clausus lápide
Custodítur sub mílite,
Triúmphans pompa nóbili,
Victor surgit de fúnere.

<h>S</h>olútis jam gemítibus,
Et inférni dolóribus,
Quia surréxit Dóminus,
Respléndens clamat Ángelus.

<h>Q</h>uǽsumus, Auctor ómnium,
In hoc pascháli gáudio,
Ab omni mortis ímpetu
Tuum defénde pópulum.

<h>G</h>lória tibi Dómine,
Qui surrexísti a mórtuis,
Cum Patre et Sancto Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
2f37d98191:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>O</c> thou, the heavens' eternal King,
Creator, unto thee we sing,
With God the Father ever One,
Co-equal, co-eternal Son.

<h>T</h>hy hand, when first the world began,
Made in thine own pure image man,
And linked to Adam, sprung from earth,
A living soul of heavenly birth.

<h>A</h>nd when by craft the envious foe
Had marred thy noblest work below,
Clothed in our flesh, thou didst restore
The image thou hadst made before.

<h>S</h>o that thou might redeem man
Whom thou hadst made
And us to God might thou wouldst unite
Through thy union with the flesh.

<h>O</h>nce wast thou born of Mary's womb;
And now, new-born from out the tomb,
O Christ, thou bidd'st us rise with thee
From death to immortality.

<h>E</h>ternal Shepherd, thou dost lave
Thy flock in pure baptismal wave,
That mystic bath, that grave of sin,
Where ransomed souls new life begin.

<h>R</h>edeemer, thou for us didst deign
To hang upon the Cross of pain,
And give for us the lavish price
Of thine own blood in sacrifice.

<h>G</h>rant, Lord, in thee each faithful mind
Unceasing paschal joy may find;
And from the death of sin set free
Souls newly born to life by thee.

<h>T</h>o Thee Who, dead, again dost live,
All glory, Lord, Thy people give;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Rom 6</r>
<c>C</c>hristus resúrgens ex mórtuis jam non móritur, mors illi ultra non dominábitur. Quod enim mórtuus est peccáto, mórtuus est semel: quod autem vivit, vivit Deo.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>S</c>ermóne blando Angelus
Predíxit muliéribus:
In Galilǽa Dóminus
Vidéndus est quantócius.

<h>I</h>llæ dum pergunt cóncite
Apóstolis hoc dícere,
Vidéntes eum vívere,
Osculántur pedes Dómini.

<h>Q</h>uo ágnito discípuli
In Galilǽam própere
Pergunt vidére fáciem
Desiderátam Dómini.

<h>C</h>laro pascháli gáudio
Sol mundo nitet rádio,
Cum Christum jam Apóstoli
Visu cernunt corpóreo.

<h>O</h>sténsa sibi vúlnera,
In Christi carne fúlgida,
Resurrexísse Dóminum
Voce faténtur pública.

<h>R</h>ex Christe clementíssime,
Tu corda nostra pósside:
Ut tibi laudes débitas
Reddámus omni témpore.

<h>Q</h>uǽsumus, Auctor ómnium,
In hoc pascháli gáudio,
Ab omni mortis ímpetu
Tuum defénde pópulum.

<h>G</h>lória tibi Dómine,
Qui surrexísti a mórtuis,
Cum Patre et Sancto Spíritu
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Gavísi sunt discípuli, allelúja.
<r>℟.</r> Viso Dómino, allelúja.
851426682b:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Rom 6</r>
<c>K</c>nowing that Christ rising again from the dead, dieth now no more, death shall no more have dominion over him. For in that he died to sin, he died once; but in that he liveth, he liveth unto God.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>T</c>he morn had spread her crimson rays,
When rang the skies with shouts of praise;
Earth joined the joyful hymn to swell,
That brought despair to vanquished hell.

<h>H</h>e comes victorious from the grave,
The Lord omnipotent to save,
And brings with him to light of day
The saints who long imprisoned lay.

<h>V</h>ain is the cavern’s three-fold ward —
The stone, the seal, the armed guard;
O death, no more thine arm we fear,
The Victor’s tomb is now thy bier.

<h>L</h>et hymns of joy to grief succeed,
We know that Christ is risen indeed;
We hear his white-robed angel’s voice,
And in our risen Lord rejoice.

<h>W</h>ith Christ we died, with Christ we rose,
When at the font his name we chose;
Oh, let not sin our robes defile,
And turn to grief the paschal smile.

<h>T</h>o God the Father let us sing,
To God the Son, our risen King,
And equally let us adore
The Spirit, God forevermore.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> The disciples were glad, alleluia.
<r>℟.</r> When they see the Lord, alleluia.

<c>A</c>d cenam Agni próvidi,
Et stolis albis cándidi,
Post tránsitum maris Rubri,
Christo canámus Príncipi.

<h>C</h>uius corpus sanctíssimum,
In ara crucis tórridum,
Cruóre ejus róseo
Gustándo vívimus Deo.

<h>P</h>rotécti Paschæ véspere
A devastánte Angelo,
Erépti de duríssimo
Pharaónis império.

<h>I</h>am Pascha nostrum Christus est,

<h>O</h> vere digna hóstia,

<h>C</h>onsúrgit Christus túmulo,
Victor redit de bárathro,
Tyránnum trudens vínculo,

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>A</c>t the Lamb’s high feast we sing
Praise to our victorious King,
Who hath washed us in the tide
Flowing from his piercèd side.

<h>P</h>raise we him whose love divine
Gives the guests his blood for wine,
Gives his body for the feast,
Love the victim, love the priest.

<h>W</h>here the paschal blood is poured,
Death’s dark angel sheathes his sword;
Israel’s hosts triumphant go
Through the wave that drowns the foe.

<h>C</h>hrist, the Lamb whose blood was shed,
Paschal victim, paschal bread;
With sincerity and love
Eat we manna from above.

<h>M</h>ighty victim from the sky,
Powers of hell beneath thee lie;
Death is conquered in the fight;
Thou hast brought us life and light.

<h>N</h>ow thy banner thou dost wave;
Vanquished Satan and the grave;
Angels join his praise to tell —
See o’erthrown the prince of hell.

<h>P</h>aschal triumph, paschal joy,
Only sin can this destroy;
From the death of sin set free,
Souls re-born, dear Lord, in Thee.

<h>H</h>ymns of glory, songs of praise,
Father, unto thee we raise;
Risen Lord, all praise to thee,
Ever with the Spirit be.
Amen.

<r>℟.</r> Because it is towards evening, alleluia.

<r>Ecclesiasticus 14:22-27</r>
Blessed is the man that shall continue in wisdom, and that shall meditate in his justice, and in his mind shall think of the all seeing eye of God. He that considereth her ways in his heart, and hath understanding in her secrets, who goeth after her as one that traceth, and stayeth in her ways: He who looketh in at her windows, and hearkeneth at her door: He that lodgeth near her house, and fastening a pin in her walls shall set up his tent nigh unto her, where good things shall rest in his lodging for ever. He shall set his children under her shelter, and shall lodge under her branches: He shall be protected under her covering from the heat, and shall rest in her glory.
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<c>p</c>ost Oríonas, Hýadum nómine, nisi Doctóres sanctæ Ecclésiæ designántur? <c>a</c> atec immérito Doctóres sancti Hýadum nuncupatióne signántur. Græco quippe elóquio hýetos plúvia vocátur, et Hýades nomen a plúviis accepérunt, quia ortæ procul dúbio imbres ferunt. Bene ergo Hýadum appellatióne expréssi sunt, qui, ad statum universális Ecclésiæ quasi in cæli fáciem dedúcti, super aréntem terram humáni péctoris, sanctæ prædicatiónis imbres fudérunt. Si enim prædicatiónis sermo plúvia non esset, Móyses mínime dixísset: Exspectétur sicut plúvia elóquium meum; et nequáquam per Isaíam Véritas díceret: Doctoris. dabo núbibus meis, ne pluant super eam imbrem; atque hoc, quod paulo ante protúlimus: Quam ob rem prohíbitæ sunt stellæ pluviárum.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>J</c>esu, the world’s Redeemer, O hear;
thy bishops’ fadeless crown, draw near:
Accept with gentlest love today
The prayers and praises that we pay.

<h>T</h>he meek confessor of thy name
Today attained a glorious fame;
Whose yearly feast, in solemn state,
Thy faithful people celebrate.

<h>T</h>he world and all its boasted good,
As vain and passing, he eschewed;
And therefore with angelic bands,
In endless joy forever stands.

<h>G</h>rant then that we, most gracious God,
May follow in the steps he trod:
And, at his prayer, thy servants free
From stain of all iniquity.

<h>P</h>aschal triumph, paschal joy,
Only sin can this destroy;
From the death of sin set free,
Souls re-born, dear Lord, in Thee.

<h>H</h>ymns of glory, songs of praise,
Father, unto thee we raise;
Risen Lord, all praise to thee,
Ever with the Spirit be.
Amen.

<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Eccli. 45</r>
<c>D</c>iléctus Deo et homínibus, cujus memória in benedictióne est: símilem illum fecit in glória sanctórum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> De ore prudéntis procédit mel, allelúja: dulcédo mellis est lingua ejus, allelúja: * Favus distíllans lábia ejus, Allelúja, allelúja.
<r>℣.</r> Sapiéntia requiéscit in corde ejus, et prudéntia in sermóne oris illíus. Favus distíllans.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Allelúja, allelúja.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>I</c>ste Conféssor Dómini sacrátus,
Festa plebs cujus celébrat per orbem,
Hódie lætus méruit secréta
Scándere cæli.

<h>Q</h>ui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbrius, castus fuit et quiétus,
Vita dum præsens vegetávit ejus
Córporis artus.

<h>O</h>b sacrum cujus túmulum frequénter
Membra languéntum modo sanitáti,
Quólibet morbo fúerint graváta,
Restituúntur.

<h>U</h>nde nunc noster chorus in honórem
Ipsius, hymnum canit hunc libénter:
Ut piis ejus méritis iuvémur
Omne per ævum.

<h>S</h>it salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui supra cæli résidens cacúmen,
Tótius mundi máchinam gubérnat
Trinus et unus.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Amávit eum Dóminus, et ornávit eum, allelúja.
<r>℟.</r> Stolam glóriæ índuit eum, allelúja.
79ea3b4352:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Eccli. 45</r>
<c>D</c>iléctus Deo et homínibus, cujus memória in benedictióne est: símilem illum fecit in glória sanctórum.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> From the mouth of the wise doth proceed honey, alleluia: the sweetness of honey is under his tongue, alleluia. * His lips drop as the honey-comb, alleluia, alleluia.
<r>℣.</r> Wisdom doth abide in his heart, and out of his mouth cometh understanding.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>T</c>his the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

<h>S</h>aintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

<h>S</h>ick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.

<h>W</h>hence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

<h>H</h>is be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Amávit eum Dóminus, et ornávit eum, allelúja.
<r>℟.</r> Stolam glóriæ índuit eum, allelúja.

<h>Lectio i</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<n>Lectio (in præparatione).</n>
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Responsorium i</h>
<r>℟.</r> Beátus vir, qui métuit Dóminum, allelúja: * In mandátis ejus cupit nimis, allelúja, allelúja, allelúja.
<r>℣.</r> Potens in terra erit semen ejus: generátio rectórum benedicétur. In mandátis ejus.
6166250ec1:
<h>Lesson 1</h>
<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May the everlasting Father bless us with an everlasting blessing.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<n>Lesson (in preparation).</n>
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>Responsory</h>
<r>℟.</r> Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord, alleluia. * He shall delight exceedingly in his commandments, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.
<r>℣.</r> His seed shall be mighty upon earth: the generation of the righteous shall be blessed.
fc5f90ed0a:
<h>Lectio ii</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adjuváre dignétur.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<n>Lectio (in præparatione).</n>
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Responsorium ii</h>
<r>℟.</r> De ore prudéntis procédit mel, allelúja: dulcédo mellis est lingua ejus, allelúja: * Favus distíllans lábia ejus, Allelúja, allelúja.
<r>℣.</r> Sapiéntia requiéscit in corde ejus, et prudéntia in sermóne oris illíus. Favus distíllans lábia.
ece2e4889c:
<h>Lesson 2</h>
<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May the only-begotten Son of God vouchsafe to bless and help us.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<n>Lesson (in preparation).</n>
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>Responsory</h>
<r>℟.</r> From the mouth of the wise doth proceed honey, alleluia: the sweetness of honey is under his tongue, alleluia. * His lips drop as the honey-comb, alleluia, alleluia.
<r>℣.</r> Wisdom doth abide in his heart, and out of his mouth cometh understanding.
602c4be254:

<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.

<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<n>Lectio (in præparatione).</n>
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Fíliæ Jerúsalem, veníte, et vidéte Mártyrem cum coróna, qua coronávit eum Dóminus * In die solemnitátis et lætítiæ, Allelúja.
<r>℣.</r> Índuit illum Dóminus stolam glóriæ, et coronávit eum. In die.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Allelúja.

<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<n>S. Vincéntii Ferrérii Conf. O.P.</n>
<r>Ant.</r> Glorióse Pater o Vincénti, cui arcem scandhnti polórum cum honóre dbvius ingénti plaudens venit chorus angelórum : canéntes te duc laude frequénti ad amœna regna Beatórum, allelúja.
<r>℣.</r> Amávit eum Dóminus, et ornávit eum, allelúja.
<r>℟.</r> Stolam glóriæ índuit eum, allelúja.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, qui géntium multitúdinem nnra beáti Vincentii Confessóris tui prædicatióne ad agnitiónem tui nóminis veníre tribuísti: præsta, quǽsumus, ut quem ventúrum Júdicem nuntiávit in terris, praemiatorem habére mereámur in cælis: Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum Fílium tuum, qui tecum vivit... T Quando hæc Oratio dicitur ad Memóriam et eam séquitur ália Memória, sic concluditur: praemiatorem habére mereámur in cælis: Christum Dóminum nostrum. 1$. Amen. Per Dóminum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

fe91b07a13: <n>From the chapter, of the following feast: B. Antónii Pavónii Mart. O.P..</n>
ac7f6ce845:
<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Jac. 1</r>
<c>B</c>eátus vir, qui suffert tentatiónem: quóniam, cum probátus fúerit, accípiet corónam vitæ, quam repromísit Deus diligéntibus se.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> De ore prudéntis procédit mel, allelúja: dulcédo mellis est lingua ejus, allelúja: * Favus distíllans lábia ejus, Allelúja, allelúja.
<r>℣.</r> Sapiéntia requiéscit in corde ejus, et prudéntia in sermóne oris illíus. Favus distíllans.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Allelúja, allelúja.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>D</c>eus tuórum mílitum
Sors, et córona, prǽmium,
Laudes canéntes Mártyris
Absólve nexu críminis.

<h>H</h>ic nempe mundi gáudia,
Et blandiménta nóxia
Cadúca rite députans,
Pervénit ad cæléstia.

<h>P</h>œnas cucúrrit fórtiter,
Et sústulit viríliter,
Pro te effúndens sánguinem,
Ætérna dona póssidet.

<h>O</h>b hoc precátu súpplici
Te póscimus, piíssime;
In hoc triúmpho Mártyris
Dimítte noxam sérvulis.

<h>Q</h>uǽsumus, Auctor ómnium,
In hoc Paschali gáudio,
Ab omni mortis ímpetu
Tuum defénde pópulum.

<h>G</h>lória tibi, Dómine,
Qui surrexísti a mórtuis,
Cum Patre et Sancto Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Glória et honóre coronásti eum, Dómine, allelúja.
<r>℟.</r> Et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum, allelúja.
a16519dd12:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Jac. 1</r>
<c>B</c>lessed is the man that endureth temptation; for when he hath been proved, he shall receive a crown of life, which God hath promised to them that love him.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> From the mouth of the wise doth proceed honey, alleluia: the sweetness of honey is under his tongue, alleluia. * His lips drop as the honey-comb, alleluia, alleluia.
<r>℣.</r> Wisdom doth abide in his heart, and out of his mouth cometh understanding.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>O</c> God, of those that fought thy fight,
Portion, and prize, and crown of light,
Break every bond of sin and shame
As now we praise thy martyr's name.

<h>H</h>e recked not of the world's allure,
But sin and pomp of sin forswore:
Knew all their gall, and passed them by,
And reached the throne prepared on high.

<h>B</h>ravely the course of pain he ran,
And bare his torments as a man:
For love of thee his blood outpoured,
And thus obtained the great reward.

<h>W</h>ith humble voice and suppliant word
We pray thee therefore, holy Lord,
While we thy martyr's feast-day keep,
Forgive thy loved and erring sheep.

<h>P</h>aschal triumph, paschal joy,
Only sin can this destroy;
From the death of sin set free,
Souls re-born, dear Lord, in Thee.

<h>H</h>ymns of glory, songs of praise,
Father, unto thee we raise;
Risen Lord, all praise to thee,
Ever with the Spirit be.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Glória et honóre coronásti eum, Dómine, allelúja.
<r>℟.</r> Et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum, allelúja.

<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus qui, ad unitátem fídei promovendam, beáto Antonio Mártyri tuo invíctam ánimi fortitúdinem contulísti: da nobis, quǽsumus, ita ejus vestígia sectári, ut finem fídei nostiæ salútem animárum reportamus. Per Dóminum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>D</c>eus tuórum mílitum
Sors, et córona, prǽmium,
Laudes canéntes Mártyris
Absólve nexu críminis.

<h>H</h>ic nempe mundi gáudia,
Et blandiménta nóxia
Cadúca rite députans,
Pervénit ad cæléstia.

<h>P</h>œnas cucúrrit fórtiter,
Et sústulit viríliter,
Pro te effúndens sánguinem,
Ætérna dona póssidet.

<h>O</h>b hoc precátu súpplici
Te póscimus, piíssime;
In hoc triúmpho Mártyris
Dimítte noxam sérvulis.

<h>Q</h>uǽsumus, Auctor ómnium,
In hoc Paschali gáudio,
Ab omni mortis ímpetu
Tuum defénde pópulum.

<h>G</h>lória tibi, Dómine,
Qui surrexísti a mórtuis,
Cum Patre et Sancto Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
a2c9b14252:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>O</c> God, of those that fought thy fight,
Portion, and prize, and crown of light,
Break every bond of sin and shame
As now we praise thy martyr's name.

<h>H</h>e recked not of the world's allure,
But sin and pomp of sin forswore:
Knew all their gall, and passed them by,
And reached the throne prepared on high.

<h>B</h>ravely the course of pain he ran,
And bare his torments as a man:
For love of thee his blood outpoured,
And thus obtained the great reward.

<h>W</h>ith humble voice and suppliant word
We pray thee therefore, holy Lord,
While we thy martyr's feast-day keep,
Forgive thy loved and erring sheep.

<h>P</h>aschal triumph, paschal joy,
Only sin can this destroy;
From the death of sin set free,
Souls re-born, dear Lord, in Thee.

<h>H</h>ymns of glory, songs of praise,
Father, unto thee we raise;
Risen Lord, all praise to thee,
Ever with the Spirit be.
Amen.

Souls re-born, dear Lord, in Thee.

<r>Actus Apostolorum 20:17-21</r>
<c>A</c> Miléto Paulus mittens Ephesum, vocávit majóres natu ecclésiæ. Qui cum veníssent ad eum, et simul essent, dixit eis: Vos scitis a prima die, qua ingréssus sum in Asiam, quáliter vobíscum per omne tempus fúerim, sérviens Dómino cum omni humilitáte, et lácrymis, et tentatiónibus, quæ mihi accidérunt ex insídiis Judæórum: quómodo nihil subtráxerim utílium, quóminus annuntiárem vobis, et docérem vos públice, et per domos, testíficans Judǽis, atque gentílibus in Deum pœniténtiam, et fidem in Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Beátus vir, qui métuit Dóminum, allelúja: * In mandátis ejus cupit nimis, allelúja, allelúja, allelúja.

<r>Actus Apostolorum 20:17-21</r>
And sending from Miletus to Ephesus, he called the ancients of the church. And when they were come to him, and were together, he said to them: You know from the first day that I came into Asia, in what manner I have been with you, for all the time, Serving the Lord with all humility, and with tears, and temptations which befell me by the conspiracies of the Jews; How I have kept back nothing that was profitable to you, but have preached it to you, and taught you publicly, and from house to house, Testifying both to Jews and Gentiles penance towards God, and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ.
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<c>Á</c>ngelo Philadelphíæ ecclésiæ scribe: Hæc dicit Sanctus et Verus, qui habet clavem David: qui áperit, nemo claudit: claudit, et nemo áperit: Scio ópera tua. Ecce dedi coram te óótium apértum, quod nemo potest cláudere: quia módicam habes virtútem, et servásti verbum meum, et non negásti nomen meum. Ecce dabo de synagóga Sátanæ, qui dicunt se Judǽos esse, et non sunt, sed mentiúntur:

be51298aa3:
<h>Lesson 1</h>
<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May the everlasting Father bless us with an everlasting blessing.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<r>Apocalypsis 3:7-9</r>
And to the angel of the church of Philadelphia, write: These things saith the Holy One and the true one, he that hath the key of David; he that openeth, and no man shutteth; shutteth, and no man openeth: I know thy works. Behold, I have given before thee a door opened, which no man can shut: because thou hast a little strength, and hast kept my word, and hast not denied my name. Behold, I will bring of the synagogue of Satan, who say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie. Behold, I will make them to come and adore before thy feet. And they shall know that I have loved thee.
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
6344c83fd2:

<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.

<c>E</c>cce fáciam illos ut véniant, et adórent ante pedes tuos: et scient quia ego diléxi te: quóniam servásti verbum patiéntiæ meæ, et ego servábo te ab hora tentatiónis, quæ ventúra est in orbem univérsum tentáre habitántes in terra. Ecce vénio cito: tene quod habes, ut nemo accípiat corónam tuam. Qui vícerit, fáciam illum colúmnam in templo Dei mei, et foras non egrediétur ámélius: et scribam super nomen Dei mei, et nomen civitátis Dei mei novæ Jerúsalem, quæ descéndit de cælo a Deo meo, et nomen meum novum.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Apocalypsis 3:9-12</r>
Behold, I will bring of the synagogue of Satan, who say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie. Behold, I will make them to come and adore before thy feet. And they shall know that I have loved thee. Because thou hast kept the word of my patience, I will also keep thee from the hour of the temptation, which shall come upon the whole world to try them that dwell upon the earth. Behold, I come quickly: hold fast that which thou hast, that no man take thy crown. He that shall overcome, I will make him a pillar in the temple of my God; and he shall go out no more; and I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, the new Jerusalem, which cometh down out of heaven from my God, and my new name.
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<c>Q</c>ui habet aurem, áudiat quid Spíritus dicat ecclésiis. Et ángelo Laodicíæ ecclésiæ scribe: Hæc dicit: Amen, testis fidélis et verus, qui est princípium creatúræ Dei. Scio ópera tua: quia neque frígidus es, neque cálidus: útinam frígidus esses, aut cálidus: sed quia tépidus es, et nec frígidus, nec cálidus, incípiam te evómere ex ore meo.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<c>T</c>his the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

<h>S</h>aintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

<h>S</h>ick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.

<h>W</h>hence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

<h>H</h>is be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

I think therefore that this is good for the present necessity, that it is good for a man so to be. Art thou bound to a wife? seek not to be loosed. Art thou loosed from a wife? seek not a wife. 9594242a85:
<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Eccli. 51</r>
<c>C</c>onfitébor tibi, Dómine Rex, et collaudábo te Deum salvatórem meum. Confitébor nómini tuo: quóniam adjútor et protéctor factus es mihi, et liberásti corpus meum a perditióne.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>I</c>esu, coróna Vírginum,
Quem Mater illa cóncipit
Quæ sola Virgo párturit,
Hæc vota clemens áccipe:

<h>Q</h>ui pascis inter lília
Septus choréis Vírginum,
Sponsus decórus glória
Sponsísque reddens prǽmia.

<h>Q</h>uocúmque pergis, Vírgines
Sequúntur, atque láudibus
Post te canéntes cúrsitant,
Hymnósque dulces pérsonant;

<h>T</h>e deprecámur lárgius,
Nostris adáuge sénsibus
Nescíre prorsus ómnia
Corruptiónis vúlnera.

<h>Q</h>uǽsumus, Auctor ómnium,
In hoc Paschali gáudio,
Ab omni mortis ímpetu
Tuum defénde pópulum.

<h>G</h>lória tibi, Dómine,
Qui surrexísti a mórtuis,
Cum Patre et Sancto Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Adducéntur regi vírgines post eam, allelúja.
<r>℟.</r> Próximæ ejus afferéntur tibi, allelúja.
6c6a58b714:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Eccli. 51</r>
<c>I</c> will give glory to thee, O Lord, O King, and I will praise thee, O God my Saviour. I will give glory to thy name: for thou hast been a helper and protector to me, and hast preserved my body from destruction.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>J</c>esu, the virgins' crown, do thou
Accept us as in prayer we bow;
Born of that Virgin, whom alone
The mother and the maid we own.

<h>A</h>mongst the lilies thou dost feed,
By virgin choirs accompanied;
With glory decked, the spotless brides
Whose bridal gifts thy love provides.

<h>T</h>hey, wheresoe'er thy footsteps bend,
With hymns and praises still attend:
In blessèd troops they follow thee,
With dance, and song, and melody.

<h>W</h>e pray thee therefore to bestow
Upon our senses here below
Thy grace, that so we may endure
From taint of all corruption pure.

<h>P</h>aschal triumph, paschal joy,
Only sin can this destroy;
From the death of sin set free,
Souls re-born, dear Lord, in Thee.

<h>H</h>ymns of glory, songs of praise,
Father, unto thee we raise;
Risen Lord, all praise to thee,
Ever with the Spirit be.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Adducéntur regi vírgines post eam, allelúja.
<r>℟.</r> Próximæ ejus afferéntur tibi, allelúja.

<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

That thou increase in our senses
To know nothing at all

<c>M</c>ódicum est hoc totum spátium, quo præsens pérvolat sǽculum. Unde dicit idem ipse Evangelísta in Epístola Octavam Pascha. sua: Novíssima hora est. Ídeo namque áédidit: Quia vado ad Patrem: quod ad priórem senténtiam referéndum est, ubi ait: Módicum et jam non vidébitis me: non ad posteriórem, ait: El íterum módicum, et vidébitis me. Eúndo quippe ad Patrem, factúrus erat ut eum non vidérent. Lectio ii, telis ergo ait: Módicum, et jam non vidébitis me; qui eum corporáliter tunc vidébant: quia itúrus erat ad Patrem, et eum deínceps mortálem visúri non erant, qualem, cum ista loquerétur, vidébant. Quod vero áédidit: Et íterum módicum, et vidébitis me: univérsæ promísit Ecclésiæ, sicut univérsæ promísit: Ecce ego vobíscum sum usque ad consummatiónem sǽculi. Non tardat Dóminus promíssum.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.

<c>N</c>ow let the earth with joy resound,

From the death of sin set free,
Souls re-born, dear Lord, in Thee.

Risen Lord, all praise to thee,
Ever with the Spirit be.

<c>N</c>ow let the earth with joy resound,

Shall judge the living and the dead,
Lights of the world forevermore!
To you the suppliant prayer we pour.

<h>Y</h>e close the sacred gates on high;
At your command apart they fly:
Oh! loose for us the guilty chain
We strive to break, and strive in vain.

At your command they go or stay:
From sin's disease our souls restore;
In good confirm us more and more.

<h>S</h>o when the world is at its end,
And Christ to judgement shall descend,
May we be called those joys to see
Prepared from all eternity.

<h>P</h>aschal triumph, paschal joy,
Only sin can this destroy;
From the death of sin set free,
Souls re-born, dear Lord, in Thee.

Father, unto thee we raise;
Risen Lord, all praise to thee,
Ever with the Spirit be.
Amen.

Et post pauca: Vidéntibus illis, elevátus est, et nubes suscépit eum ab óculis eórum. Notáte verba, signáte mystéria. Convéscens elevátus est. Comédit, et ascéndit: ut vidélicet per efféctum comestiónis, véritas patésceret carnis. Marcus vero, priúsquam cælum Dóminus ascéndat, eum de cordis atque infidelitátis durítia increpásse discípulos mémorat. Qua in re quid considerándum est, nisi quod idcírco Dóminus tunc discípulos increpávit, cum eos corporáliter relíquit, ut verba, quæ recédens díceret, in audiéntium árctius impréssa remanérent?

Now confirm to our minds the trustworthiness of the fact that our Lord did indeed rise again from the dead, it is well for us to remark one of the statements of Luke (Acts i. 4.) “Eating together with them, He commanded them that they should not (1 John xiv. 16, 17 xvi. 7.) depart from Jerusalem and a little afterward: “While they beheld, He was taken up, and a cloud received Him out of their sight.” Consider these words, note well these mysteries. After “eating together with them He was taken up.” He ate and ascended: that the fact of His eating might show the reality of the Body in Which He went up. But Mark telleth us that before the Lord ascended into heaven, He upbraided His disciples; with their unbelief and hardness of heart. From this I know not why we should gather, but that the Lord then upbraided His disciples, for whom He was about to be parted in the body, to the end that the words which He spoke unto them as He left them might be the deeper imprinted on their hearts.
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.

On the solemn Feast of the Passover the cause of our joy was that Christ was risen again. This day we rejoice because that He is ascended up into heaven. We call to mind and justly celebrate that day whereon our lowly nature was, in the Person of Christ, borne up high above all the heavenly armies, above all the circles of Angels, beyond the heights of all the Powers, even to where Christ is sitting on the right hand of the Father. Our foundations are laid, and our house is built upon this succession of the works of God and His grace is made more wonderful by this, that, though the visible Object of worship is removed from among men, the faith of the Church doth not grow weak, nor her hope wavering, nor her love cold.

<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May the everlasting Father bless us with an everlasting blessing.

From the Sermons of St Maximus, Bishop [of Turin.] It is idle to strive to add anything to the praise of our holy and most blessed Father Antoninus whose Feast is this day kept. The beauty of his life ought not to be the subject of panegyrics, so much as the object of imitation. The Scripture saith “A wise son is the glory of his father,” truly then will he be honoured by such as, by doing after his en sample, show themselves to be his children for in Christ Jesus hath he begotten us through the Gospel.(1 Cor. iv. 15.)
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>Responsory</h>
<r>℟.</r> Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord, alleluia. * He shall delight exceedingly in his commandments, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.
<r>℣.</r> His seed shall be mighty upon earth: the generation of the righteous shall be blessed.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>I</c>ste Conféssor Dómini sacrátus,
Festa plebs cujus celébrat per orbem,
Hódie lætus méruit secréta
Scándere cæli.

<h>Q</h>ui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbrius, castus fuit et quiétus,
Vita dum præsens vegetávit ejus
Córporis artus.

<h>O</h>b sacrum cujus túmulum frequénter
Membra languéntum modo sanitáti,
Quólibet morbo fúerint graváta,
Restituúntur.

<h>U</h>nde nunc noster chorus in honórem
Ipsius, hymnum canit hunc libénter:
Ut piis ejus méritis iuvémur
Omne per ævum.

<h>S</h>it salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui supra cæli résidens cacúmen,
Tótius mundi máchinam gubérnat
Trinus et unus.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>T</c>his the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

<h>S</h>aintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

<h>S</h>ick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.

<h>W</h>hence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

<h>H</h>is be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> The Lord loved him and beautified him.
<r>℟.</r> He clothed him with a robe of glory.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>I</c>ste Conféssor Dómini sacrátus,
Festa plebs cujus celébrat per orbem,
Hódie lætus méruit secréta
Scándere cæli.

<h>Q</h>ui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbrius, castus fuit et quiétus,
Vita dum præsens vegetávit ejus
Córporis artus.

<h>O</h>b sacrum cujus túmulum frequénter
Membra languéntum modo sanitáti,
Quólibet morbo fúerint graváta,
Restituúntur.

<h>U</h>nde nunc noster chorus in honórem
Ipsius, hymnum canit hunc libénter:
Ut piis ejus méritis iuvémur
Omne per ævum.

<h>S</h>it salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui supra cæli résidens cacúmen,
Tótius mundi máchinam gubérnat
Trinus et unus.
Amen.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>T</c>his the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

<h>S</h>aintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

<h>S</h>ick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.

Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.

<c>e</c>nim quantum in ænígmate infírmitas humána óculum mentis in æternitáte fígere potest, quanta sint supérnæ civitátis gáudia: et ea enarráre non suffíciens admirándo clamábat Quid mihi est in cælo? Quasi díceret: Excédit vires meas, excédit facultátem eloquéntiæ meæ, transcéndit capacitátem intelligéntiæ meæ illud decus, illa glória, illa celsitúdo, qua nobis, a conturbatióne hóminum remótis, in abscóndito faciéi suæ Jesus Christus Dóminus noster reformábit corpus humilitátis nostræ, configurátum córpori claritátis suæ. Hujus perféctæ libertátis contemplatióne nullum vitábat perículum, nullum horrébat supplícium: et si mílies posset mori, non putábat se hanc digne posse áliqua ratióne promeréri. Iii. Nocturno. Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.

<h>Responsorium vi</h>
<r>℟.</r> Hic est vere Martyr, qui pro Christi nómine sánguinem suum fudit: * Qui minas júdicum non tímuit, nec terrénæ dignitátis glóriam quæsívit, Sed ad cæléstia regna pervénit.

d08fae728a:
<h>Lesson 6</h>
<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May God kindle in our hearts the fire of his love.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
For he considered, as far as man's weakness is able, through this darkness, to fix the eyes of his mind upon the eternal things, what is the gladness of the city above and being not able to tell it, he cried out wondering “What have I in heaven?” As though he would have said “It passeth my strength, it passeth the power of my utterance, it goeth beyond the reach of my understanding, what is that beauty, what is that glory, what is that exaltation, wherein, when He hath hidden us from the troubling of men, in the secret of His presence, our Lord Jesus Christ shall change our vile body, that it may be fashioned like unto His glorious Body” (Ps. xxx. 21, Phil. iii. 21.) In sight of this perfect liberty he shrank from no danger, and quailed before no suffering and if he could have died a thousand times, he would not have thought himself to have bought it at a price high enough.
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> This is a Martyr indeed, who shed his blood for Christ's Name's sake * Who feared not for the threats of judges, nor sought to be great with the glory of this world, but pressed on unto the kingdom of heaven.

Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

<c>O</c> God, of those that fought thy fight,
Portion, and prize, and crown of light,
Break every bond of sin and shame
As now we praise thy martyr's name.

<h>H</h>e recked not of the world's allure,
But sin and pomp of sin forswore:
Knew all their gall, and passed them by,
And reached the throne prepared on high.

<h>B</h>ravely the course of pain he ran,
And bare his torments as a man:
For love of thee his blood outpoured,
And thus obtained the great reward.

<h>W</h>ith humble voice and suppliant word
We pray thee therefore, holy Lord,
While we thy martyr's feast-day keep,
Forgive thy loved and erring sheep.

<h>G</h>lory and praise for aye be done
To God the Father, and the Son,
And Holy Ghost, who reign on high,
One God, to all eternity.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>I</c>ste Conféssor Dómini sacrátus,
Festa plebs cujus celébrat per orbem,
Hódie lætus méruit secréta
Scándere cæli.

<h>Q</h>ui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbrius, castus fuit et quiétus,
Vita dum præsens vegetávit ejus
Córporis artus.

<h>O</h>b sacrum cujus túmulum frequénter
Membra languéntum modo sanitáti,
Quólibet morbo fúerint graváta,
Restituúntur.

<h>U</h>nde nunc noster chorus in honórem
Ipsius, hymnum canit hunc libénter:
Ut piis ejus méritis iuvémur
Omne per ævum.

<h>S</h>it salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui supra cæli résidens cacúmen,
Tótius mundi máchinam gubérnat
Trinus et unus.
Amen.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>T</c>his the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

<h>S</h>aintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

<h>S</h>ick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.

<h>W</h>hence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

<h>H</h>is be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.
